To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). **Project Kestrel: Seller draft reviewed against Buyer playbook**

The Seller's note calls its positions "FINAL" and says principal-level settlement is done. Nothing in the file shows Amelia Frost approved any of them, so the playbook governs. Where the Seller's draft sits at the 20%/AUD 4.8M cap, that is our conditional fallback, which requires her prior written authority. None has been given.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000) for general Warranty Claims (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer should want:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% fallback is usable only with Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and hold at 25%. Do not concede 20% without written authority.
- **Reason:** The fallback needs principal approval that has not been given.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket; only the excess above the basket is recoverable (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer should want:** AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 aggregate basket; seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject both figures and the deductible structure.
- **Reason:** The Seller's proposal is roughly five times our de minimis and five times our basket, and it converts a tipping basket into a deductible.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion (cl 12.3/13), and any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly excluded.
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months after Completion for general claims. 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 18 months; hold at 24. Reject the "applies to all Claims" wording.
- **Reason:** The 18-month figure needs approval we do not have, and the cross-application would drag other regimes down to the general period.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer should want:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright.
- **Reason:** Title and capacity are core to what we are buying, so they cannot sit under a 20% cap and 18-month limit.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). No fraud carve-out is offered.
- **Buyer should want:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Insert the carve-out expressly.
- **Reason:** As drafted, the Seller's clauses would reach fraud, which is non-negotiable under the playbook.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (including DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2).
- **Buyer should want:** Specific, fair disclosure only. No whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 1.1 and 1.2 and require specific disclosure against specific warranties.
- **Reason:** Blanket disclosure would neutralise most warranty claims, since almost any matter can be found somewhere in the data room.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and delete cl 8.3 as drafted.
- **Reason:** A "discoverable from the data room" test would shift risk to us for everything we reviewed, including the specific issues flagged in the Disclosure Letter.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). The Disclosure Letter confirms no final written consent or evidence of conditions is in the file.
- **Buyer should want:** Effective consent and evidence that its conditions (DD-002 cl 11.3) are satisfied before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Make effective consent plus condition satisfaction a Completion condition.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue, and the Seller's delivery-based wording could let Completion proceed without an effective consent.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2M outstanding, to be addressed by a release provided after Completion (cl 2/7). The Disclosure Letter confirms the facility has not been repaid.
- **Buyer should want:** A current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-completion release. Require repayment and releases at Completion.
- **Reason:** Leaving AUD 3.2M of secured debt in place after Completion leaves us exposed to the lender and the security.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. The Disclosure Letter says on-costs (payroll tax, super) are not stated.
- **Buyer should want:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs shown as a specific line item, or seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Add a specific funds-flow line for bonuses plus on-costs, or make it seller-funded, and quantify on-costs.
- **Reason:** Unrecorded Completion-triggered payments would fall to the Company after Completion.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. This is not independent bank verification either way. No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Buyer should want:** A broadened indemnity covering the Ironquay IP matter, with the SOW3 cure preserved. The AUD 180,000 must not be treated as confirmed debt or as cleared.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow indemnity. Broaden it while preserving the cure mechanism.
- **Reason:** Limiting the indemnity to one SOW payment leaves the IP transfer risk (cl 7.3 cleared payment condition) uncovered.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter" not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). The Disclosure Letter does not characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss.
- **Buyer should want:** No assumption of confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand, in either direction. Preserve logs, investigate, and require regular updates.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept "not material." Require log preservation, investigation scope, and updates, and escalate to Amelia Frost for any specific protection.
- **Reason:** About 1,240 records with personal data are potentially exposed, and the investigation is incomplete.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- **Seller:** Three renewals are "ordinary-course operating costs" (no Debt classification sought).
- **Buyer should want:** Assessment only. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction. Confirm whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Recommendation:** Accept as an item for assessment, not as a settled ordinary-course cost. Request the renewal terms and timing.
- **Reason:** The Disclosure Letter does not say whether the renewals are terminable or accrued, so we cannot confirm the Seller's characterisation.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Collapses Title, Tax, IP and capacity into the general regime (Fundamental/Title and "all Claims" wording).
- **Buyer should want:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Restore separate regimes for each category.
- **Reason:** The Seller's "administrative simplicity" argument would move every high-risk category under the 20% cap and 18-month limit.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012 (Disclosure Letter item 10).
- **Buyer should want:** Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is a supplied internal source and is not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as sufficient evidence. Require independent verification before signing, such as official registry searches, PPSR searches, and evidence of the transfer and authority for the Seller.
- **Reason:** The share register is maintained by the Company or Seller, so it cannot independently prove title.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months).
- **Buyer should want:** Tax and IP terms remain open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution until negotiated.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Keep Tax and IP open and outside the general regime.
- **Reason:** Settling them under the general regime would cap and time-limit tax and IP exposures that are not yet quantified.

---

**Approvals and next steps**
- Only Amelia Frost can approve any fallback (20% cap, 18-month period, or a post-completion Riverlark release). None has been given.
- Information requests: Bluefen consent and conditions evidence; Riverlark payout and releases; bonus on-costs; Sandbar renewal terms; DD-006 investigation scope and logs; independent title searches; Ironquay SOW3 payment and assignment records.
